info.title: AMOS API
info.description: API for Analytical Methods & Open Spectra (AMOS). JSON operations require Content-Type: application/json; uploads require multipart/form-data with a real file part. Use POST for searches with request bodies. A browser address-bar request uses GET and cannot invoke a POST operation. Path examples illustrate identifier syntax and do not guarantee that a record exists in the selected deployment. Pagination cursors are opaque tokens returned by the server; omit the cursor for the first page. Metadata PUT operations write data and may clear omitted metadata or substance associations: fetch the editor information and submit the intended complete values. File ingestion performs PDF processing/OCR and indexing synchronously; a client timeout does not prove that an upload failed. Check for the created record before retrying. All error responses use application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id. Legacy error/ issues fields are retained for client errors. Every response includes X-Request-ID. Server errors omit internal exception details. Failed requests roll back uncommitted database work; an already committed upload cannot be undone by a later processing failure. Do not automatically retry writes after a timeout or connection loss.

post.summary: Returns information on a batch of fact sheets specified by internal ID.

400.description: Invalid request fields, cursor, or document type. Returns application/problem+json with request_id; legacy error and issues fields are retained when present.

200.description: A list of information on the submitted batch of fact sheets.

schema.description: JSON response. The exact fields depend on the selected record type and data source.

415.description: Request rejected. Use the documented Content-Type. Returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id; legacy error and issues fields are preserved.

204.description: No internal IDs were selected. Empty response body.

500.description: An unexpected server error occurred. Returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id. X-Request-ID identifies the corresponding server log entry.

502.description: An upstream HTTP/search service failed or returned an unusable response. Returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id. X-Request-ID identifies the corresponding server log entry.

503.description: The database connection or transaction is temporarily unavailable or busy. Returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id. X-Request-ID identifies the corresponding server log entry.

504.description: An upstream service exceeded its connection or read timeout. Returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and request_id. X-Request-ID identifies the corresponding server log entry.
